sections.body: Grant proposals and funding is the part of AI research where machine learning helps with the paperwork and strategy around money. AI systems now read past proposals and papers to suggest text, check a draft against a funder's formatting rules, and flag missing sections before submission. They can build budget drafts from line items and known allowable cost rules, and they can scan publication and project databases to suggest potential collaborators. They can also estimate how a proposal might score by comparing it with funded and unfunded examples. These tools do not write a winning proposal on their own, but they reduce the time spent on repetitive checks and searches. The work is practical, focused on documents, rules, and patterns rather than on making scientific judgments.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are well solved, especially format checking and basic budget arithmetic. A system can reliably catch a font size error, a missing biographical sketch, or a cost that exceeds a stated cap. Finding collaborators is partly solved, because search and recommendation can surface names from coauthorship and topic similarity. Predicting proposal success is not solved in any dependable way, because review outcomes depend on panel dynamics, program priorities, and unstated factors that are not in the text. Drafting help is useful for structure and phrasing, but it can produce confident text that is wrong about the science or the funder's intent. The honest limit is that these tools assist human judgment, they do not replace it, and they cannot guarantee funding.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section follow the proposal lifecycle. Drafting Proposals from Past Work covers how to reuse and adapt earlier writing, and the site's library of 135 research papers can be a source of material for that step. Funder Formatting and Compliance deals with the rules that decide whether a proposal is even reviewed, while Budgets and Allowable Costs explains how to build a budget that matches agency rules. Finding Collaborators looks at how to identify partners and assemble a team, and Predicting Proposal Success examines attempts to forecast review outcomes from text and metadata. A reader who wants to understand the whole pipeline can move through them in that order, or go straight to the page that matches the immediate task. Together they show where AI helps, where it only assists, and where the evidence is still thin.
